topic.readerProblem: A buyer wants to know whether LLMrefs is worth paying for, what its free plan really includes, whether the single $79 per month plan fits, and whether it shows the actual AI answers.
topic.connection: AEOeye audits whether AI engines recommend a brand; this page helps buyers decide between a keyword-level tracker and first reading real answers, using only public documentation.

assessment: The page is documentation-based and says so near the top. It reports what LLMrefs publishes on its pricing card, FAQ and product pages (one $79 per month plan, 500 prompts, weekly refresh, 7-day trial, 'Limited time only' label), states plainly that the free plan limits are not published, flags LLMrefs' own pages disagreeing on refresh cadence, and treats the 2/5 data-accuracy rating as one dated opinion from a competing agency. It does not claim hands-on testing, does not state a free-plan keyword limit as fact, and does not repeat the earlier Enterprise tier or daily-refresh claims that no current LLMrefs page supports.

sources.supports: Pricing card ($79/month, 500 prompts, 7-day trial, 'Limited time only', weekly reports, unlimited seats/projects, CSV/API, extras), FAQ (engines, at-least-weekly refresh, 'more than 50 keywords' upgrade), keywords-not-prompts approach, non-determinism remark, Rankings/Prompts/Sources mockup, London address in JSON-LD
LLMrefs page stating it generates and runs prompts daily, contradicting the weekly cadence on the pricing card
LLMrefs' own comparison table listing 'Free plan; Pro $79/mo for 50 keywords' with no free-plan limits
Otterly.ai Lite $29/month (15 prompts) and Standard $189/month (100 prompts), four engines on every plan with Claude, AI Mode and Gemini as add-ons, daily tracking
Dated (November 2025) hands-on opinion from an AI SEO agency: data accuracy 2/5, keyword-level reporting hides which prompt triggered a mention, domain citations reliably flagged versus manual checks
Share of voice defined in advertising as a company's share of total category spend
